# From Thawr to Qubāʾ: seven messages for the WhatsApp pilot (experiment X6)
# Draft. Not reviewed. A teacher reads each one before it is sent.

Day 1
From Thawr to Qubāʾ. Today we stand at Qubāʾ. Madinah is 4 km to the north, in a straight line.

Day 2
The text says: "twelve nights gone of Rabīʿ al-Awwal, on a Monday, when the forenoon heat grew strong and the sun had nearly reached its height" (Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, vol. 1, p. 492). Question for tomorrow: what would the moon have looked like that night?

Day 3
Computed, not reported: on the modern calendar's reckoning (Friday 24 September 622) the moon was 97% lit. The date conversion itself is uncertain, so scholars keep the reported date and the converted one apart.

Day 4
The text names 22 places on the road from Makkah to Qubāʾ. Only 4 can be placed on a map today. Guess which.

Day 5
The text gives the weekday: Monday. None of the three computed lunations falls on that weekday under a simple crescent rule: a question for the scholars.

Day 6
The text names 3 people at this event.

Day 7
Three questions, from memory:
1. From Qubāʾ, which way does Madinah lie?
2. The text names 22 places from Makkah to Qubāʾ. How many can be placed on a map here?
3. On which weekday does the text place it?
